target.title: fix(discord): gate guild metadata reads [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who configured Discord read allowlists could still have guild-level metadata read through Discord action tools when an arbitrary guild or channel ID was supplied.

AI-assisted change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord guild metadata and thread-list read paths now use the same read-target authorization checks as message reads. Guild-wide metadata reads require the guild to be allowed without narrowing to a single channel, while channel-specific metadata reads continue to authorize the concrete channel target.

This keeps Discord admin/mutation permission checks unchanged and does not add config, storage, provider, or migration surfaces.

## User Impact

Operators can expect Discord metadata tools to respect the configured read allowlist consistently. Allowed channel reads and guild-wide reads with a wildcard channel allowlist continue to work; non-allowlisted guilds or channels are rejected before the Discord API read runs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 111 tests.


### Exact-head OpenClaw Discord action proof

Head: `95c59ff92550ba21dd6c3763251fcd888017cad9`

Real setup: ran the production Discord channel message-action adapter (`discordPlugin.actions.handleAction`) from the OpenClaw PR worktree with the Discord provider/runtime surface replaced by a deterministic redacted Discord API logger. This exercises the OpenClaw message action entry point, Discord action routing, the patched read-target authorization gates, and the provider-call boundary without using live Discord credentials or private server IDs.

Proof command:

```bash
corepack pnpm exec tsx --eval '<discord message-action proof script>'
```

Redacted result:

```json
{
  "proof": "discord-read-target-openclaw-message-action",
  "head": "95c59ff92550ba21dd6c3763251fcd888017cad9",
  "ok": true,
  "scenarios": [
    {
      "name": "OpenClaw message action rejects active thread-list with only channel allowlist",
      "ok": false,
      "error": "Discord active thread lists require a wildcard channel allowlist so each read target can be authorized.",
      "providerCalls": []
    },
    {
      "name": "OpenClaw message action allows active thread-list with wildcard guild allowlist",
      "ok": true,
      "providerCalls": ["discord.listThreads"]
    },
    {
      "name": "OpenClaw message action rejects guild channel-list with only channel allowlist",
      "ok": false,
      "error": "Discord guild metadata reads require a wildcard channel allowlist for this guild.",
      "providerCalls": []
    },
    {
      "name": "OpenClaw message action allows guild channel-list with wildcard guild allowlist",
      "ok": true,
      "providerCalls": ["discord.listGuildChannels"]
    }
  ],
  "providerLog": [
    { "event": "discord.listThreads", "guildId": "guild-main", "channelId": "chan-allowed" },
    { "event": "discord.listGuildChannels", "guildId": "guild-main" }
  ]
}
```

What this proves: a channel-specific allowlist no longer authorizes guild-wide active-thread or guild-metadata reads; OpenClaw rejects before the Discord provider call. The wildcard-guild allowlist path still reaches the expected Discord provider read calls, preserving the intended allowed behavior.

Compatibility note: the fail-closed behavior for channel-specific guild allowlists is intentional. Operators who want guild-wide metadata or active-thread reads must configure a wildcard guild channel allowlist; channel-specific archived thread reads remain channel-scoped.
